subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
subcategory: Privacy Laws That Changed the World
title: Why America Has No Federal Privacy Law
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Why America Has No Federal Privacy Law.

hook.text: Europe has GDPR. America has nothing comparable. The world's tech capital has no comprehensive privacy law.

buildup.text: American privacy is regulated by a patchwork of sector-specific laws: health, finance, children, students.

discovery.text: Lobbyists from the tech industry spend hundreds of millions annually to prevent comprehensive privacy legislation.

twist.text: Both parties agree privacy law is needed. They disagree on whether it should override stronger state laws.

climax.text: America invented the internet and built Big Tech — but can't pass a law to protect its citizens' data.

punchline.text: Built the internet. Can't regulate the data.

quiz.question: What prevents the US from passing a comprehensive federal privacy law?
options: Intense lobbying and disagreements over preempting state laws
